S7 Class for the Result of an Optimization

Source: R/result_class.R
optimizer_result.Rd

The value of minimize() and maximize(): the point reached and the value there, the evaluation counts, whether the run converged and which rule stopped it, and enough of the run to diagnose it otherwise. The optimizer itself is kept on the object, so a run can be repeated from its result.

Usage

optimizer_result(
  par = integer(0),
  value = integer(0),
  gradient = NULL,
  counts = NULL,
  iterations = integer(0),
  converged = logical(0),
  criterion_met = character(0),
  message = character(0),
  trace = NULL,
  optimizer = NULL,
  elapsed = integer(0),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

par

The minimizer reached, a numeric vector of the same length as the starting point.

value

The objective at par, a single number. For a run started by maximize() this is the value of the original objective, and its sign is already undone.

gradient

The gradient at par, a numeric vector, or NULL for a method that computes none. prox_grad() reports the proximal gradient mapping here.

counts

A named integer vector of length three, f, g and h: evaluations of the objective, the gradient and the Hessian. A gradient obtained by differencing is counted in f, one per coordinate per side.

iterations

The number of iterations performed, a single integer.

converged

A single logical; see Details.

criterion_met

A single string: the label of the rule that fired, no decrease above the objective's resolution or bracket at machine resolution for the two stops described in Details, iteration budget reached or evaluation budget reached for a budget, and stopped without converging for a run that stopped for another reason.

message

A single string, empty when there is nothing to report. Carries notes such as gradient obtained by finite differences.

trace

The iteration path as a data frame, or NULL when the optimizer was built with keep_trace = FALSE, which is the default.

optimizer

The optimizer() that produced the result, kept whole so the run can be repeated or restarted from where it stopped.

elapsed

Wall-clock seconds, a single number. The time is measured to the platform's clock resolution, so a fast run can read exactly 0.

seed

The state of the random number generator when the run began, an integer vector, or NULL for a deterministic method.

Value

An S7 object of class optimizer_result carrying the twelve properties above. Built by the methods of minimize(); a caller receives one and does not construct it.

The meaning of converged

converged is TRUE when the stopping rule was satisfied, and also when a line search with a declared resolution established that every step fails to decrease the objective by more than that resolution (criterion_met is then no decrease above the objective's resolution) or when brent() reduced its bracket to the resolution of the iterate (bracket at machine resolution). Running out of iterations or evaluations leaves it FALSE and puts iteration budget reached or evaluation budget reached into criterion_met; message then reads evaluation budget exhausted for the second. A line search that finds no acceptable step also leaves it FALSE, with criterion_met equal to stopped without converging. In the methods with a line search, an accepted step that moves the iterate by no more than \(4\epsilon\max(1, \lVert x\rVert_\infty)\), with \(\epsilon\) the machine precision, is treated in the same way: the stopping rule is then evaluated without the previous iterate, so only a rule on the gradient can report convergence, and otherwise message reads the step did not move the iterate beyond rounding and the trace records step below rounding. A change in the parameters or in the objective over such a step is rounding, and it is not read as convergence. For the same reason, when the stopping rule is met on a step \(\Delta x\) along which the first-order change at the new point, \(\lvert g^\top \Delta x\rvert\), exceeds \(\max(1, \lvert f\rvert)\), the step is undone and the run is handled as above, with the message the step that met the stopping rule is not resolved by the objective and the safeguard step not resolved. A run that ends on a budget is therefore reported as not converged, so that code reading the result can distinguish it from a run that satisfied a rule.

The trace

With keep_trace = TRUE on the optimizer, trace is a data frame with one row per iteration. For a single method it has the columns iteration, value, a third column holding the quantity read by the stopping rule, step and safeguard; brent() has no step column. The third column is gnorm for a method that computes a gradient and stationarity for one that does not, so code that reads a trace should select the column by position or check names(trace). A multistart() trace has one row per start, with the columns start, value, converged and iterations, and a chain() trace has an additional stage column.

safeguard names the repair that the algorithm applied to its own step, or "none". The names differ by method; examples are step shortened and step adjusted for the line-search methods, cg restart when conjugacy is lost, bb curvature reset when a secant pair has no usable curvature, and reflect, expand, contract in and contract out for the simplex. summary() tabulates them.

Repeating a stochastic run

seed holds .Random.seed as it was when the run began, and is filled in only by the methods that draw random numbers themselves: sa(), compass() with its default directions = "mads", and multistart(). A chain() carries the seed of its first stage. adam() draws no random numbers, so its seed is NULL; a resampling objective draws in the session of the caller. Assigning the seed back reproduces the run exactly:

a <- minimize(sa(maxit = 300), f, c(-1.2, 1))
assign(".Random.seed", a@seed, globalenv())
b <- minimize(sa(maxit = 300), f, c(-1.2, 1))
identical(a@par, b@par)   # TRUE

For a deterministic method seed is NULL.

See also

minimize(), print.optimizer_result() and summary.optimizer_result() for the two views of it, plot.optimizer_result() for the trace.

Examples

f <- function(p) (1 - p[1])^2 + 100 * (p[2] - p[1]^2)^2
g <- function(p) c(-2 * (1 - p[1]) - 400 * p[1] * (p[2] - p[1]^2),
                   200 * (p[2] - p[1]^2))

res <- minimize(bfgs(keep_trace = TRUE), f, c(-1.2, 1), gr = g)
res@par
#> [1] 0.9999995 0.9999989
res@converged
#> [1] TRUE
res@criterion_met
#> [1] "gradient (max-norm) < 1e-06 or |df| < 1e-10 or |dx| < 1e-08"
res@counts
#>  f  g  h 
#> 49 39  0 

# A budget stops the run and leaves converged FALSE, with the reason in
# criterion_met.
short <- minimize(bfgs(maxit = 3), f, c(-1.2, 1), gr = g)
c(short@converged, short@criterion_met)
#> [1] "FALSE"                    "iteration budget reached"

# The name of the third column of the trace is the quantity read by the
# rule.
names(res@trace)
#> [1] "iteration" "value"     "gnorm"     "step"      "safeguard"
names(minimize(nelder_mead(keep_trace = TRUE), f, c(-1.2, 1))@trace)
#> [1] "iteration"    "value"        "stationarity" "step"         "safeguard"   

# The optimizer travels with the result, so the run can be repeated.
again <- minimize(res@optimizer, f, c(-1.2, 1), gr = g)
all.equal(again@par, res@par)
#> [1] TRUE
